content.value_statement: WordPress Interactivity API work can fail when directives, stores, and hydration do not align. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through focused debugging and implementation steps.
actual_capabilities: Recognizes WordPress Interactivity API directives and store usage in blocks, themes, and plugins.
Guides setup decisions for block view script modules and module-based frontend scripts.
Checks store state, actions, callbacks, and directive namespaces for consistency.
Explains WordPress 6.9 guidance for unique directive IDs and deprecated data-wp-ignore usage.
Provides debugging steps for inert directives, hydration mismatch, and client-side navigation issues.
Recommends verification through triage output, manual smoke tests, and Playwright tests when available.
limitations: It depends on access to the target repository and relevant block, theme, or plugin files.
It does not replace official WordPress documentation for version-specific API changes.
It cannot confirm browser behavior without running or inspecting the affected site.
It may require clarification when the build system or WordPress version is unknown.

use_cases.title: Fix Inert Directives
use_cases.description: Diagnose why rendered data-wp directives do not trigger actions or update state.

use_cases.title: Add Interactive Blocks
use_cases.description: Plan a new interactive block using view script modules and scoped store state.

use_cases.title: Review Interactivity Changes
use_cases.description: Check a pull request for hydration alignment, directive scope, and WordPress 6.9 compatibility.

prompt_templates.title: Identify API Usage
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner discovery in an existing repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Find where this project uses the WordPress Interactivity API. Summarize directives, stores, and view script module integration.

prompt_templates.title: Debug A Broken Interaction
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate troubleshooting for inert UI behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Debug why this WordPress interaction does not run. Check the interactive root, module loading, store namespace, and hydration errors.

prompt_templates.title: Implement A Scoped Change
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced feature work in an existing block
prompt_templates.prompt: Add this interactive behavior with minimal directives. Keep server markup and client state aligned, then describe verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Version Compatibility
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Interactivity API implementation for WordPress 6.9 compatibility, deprecated data-wp-ignore usage, and directive ID collisions.

output_examples.input: The button has Interactivity API directives, but clicking it does nothing.
output: A short diagnosis of likely causes, starting with module loading and namespace mismatches.
A checklist for confirming the interactive root, store registration, action name, and console errors.
A verification plan covering manual browser testing and available end-to-end tests.

output_examples.input: Review this block for WordPress 6.9 Interactivity API compatibility.
output: A compatibility review covering deprecated ignore behavior, unique directive IDs, and navigation state resets.
A prioritized list of changes with the affected markup, store behavior, and expected user impact.
A release checklist for smoke testing frontend interactions after the update.

output_examples.input: Add an interactive toggle to a server-rendered WordPress block.
output: A scoped implementation plan for markup directives, store state, and action handling.
Notes on keeping initial server output aligned with client hydration.
Suggested tests that confirm the toggle updates visible state without layout flicker.

best_practices: Start by locating existing directives, stores, and view script module wiring before changing behavior.
Keep interactive roots small and align server-rendered markup with initial client state.
Verify changes with manual interaction tests and end-to-end coverage when the project has it.
anti_patterns: Adding broad interactive roots around large page sections without a clear state boundary.
Using deprecated data-wp-ignore behavior instead of conditional rendering or separate regions.
Changing directive names without checking store namespaces, action names, and hydration output.

faq.question: What projects is this skill for?
faq.answer: It is for WordPress projects using the Interactivity API in blocks, themes, or plugins.

faq.question: Can it create a new interactive block?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide scaffold choices, directive placement, store state, and verification steps.

faq.question: Can it debug hydration problems?
faq.answer: Yes. It focuses on server markup, initial state, directive scope, and client-side errors.

faq.question: Does it require WP-CLI?
faq.answer: No. Some workflows may use WP-CLI, but the skill also supports code review and manual debugging.

faq.question: Does it support WordPress 6.9 changes?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for unique directive IDs, deprecated data-wp-ignore behavior, and navigation state resets.

faq.question: Can it guarantee browser behavior?
faq.answer: No. Browser behavior still needs site access, console inspection, and interaction testing.
